name: ONNX Runtime
production_evidence: Used in production by Microsoft (Office, Azure, Bing)
Cross-platform: Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android
strengths: Cross-platform: runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android
Graph optimizations: constant folding, node elimination, fusion (GEMM+Activation, Attention, LayerNorm, etc.)
Execution provider framework: extensible to new hardware (CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO, DirectML, etc.)
Production-proven: used by Microsoft in production services
Offline optimization: can save optimized graph to disk
weaknesses: Graph-level only: does not generate new kernels, only optimizes existing ONNX operators
No autotuning: relies on heuristics for operator selection and fusion
Limited fusion compared to Triton/Inductor: cannot fuse arbitrary operations
ONNX export: not all PyTorch/TensorFlow models export cleanly to ONNX
Performance gap: for GPU inference, ONNX Runtime typically underperforms native Triton or TensorRT kernels
notes: ONNX Runtime is a cross-platform inference runtime that optimizes and executes ONNX models. It is not a kernel compiler: it does not generate new GPU kernels, but instead applies graph-level optimizations (constant folding, node elimination, operator fusion) and partitions the graph across execution providers. The execution provider framework is its key strength: the same model can run on CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO, DirectML, or CPU by simply changing the provider configuration. For production deployment, ONNX Runtime is most valuable when cross-platform support is required (e.g., Windows + Linux + mobile). For pure GPU inference on NVIDIA hardware, TensorRT or Triton-based engines typically outperform ONNX Runtime. The graph optimizations are effective but limited compared to what Triton or Inductor can achieve: ONNX Runtime can fuse GEMM+Activation or Attention, but cannot fuse arbitrary sequences of operations into a single kernel.
